sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Mail-Order Retail with Cash on Delivery Settlement

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Republic of the Marshall Islands (unitary national jurisdiction; non-resident Business Corporation regime; no sub-state tax differentiation)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid – statutory corporate law modeled on the Delaware General Corporation Law and the Model Business Corporation Act, applied within a parliamentary republic; customary law (manit) retains residual application outside commercial statutes; official languages are English and Marshallese; no Islamic Sharia application.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association with the United States of America (including the Amended Compact of Free Association, 2023) – economic relations and trade provisions
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER) Plus – ratified regional trade and economic integration agreement
No comprehensive bilateral investment treaty or double taxation avoidance agreement is currently in force; the RMI operates a tax-neutral regime for non-resident foreign-owned corporations

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act, Title 36, Associations Law of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (as amended); AML/CFT mandates of the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) and the National Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Committee implementing FATF and Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG) standards; Registration and Beneficial Ownership Declaration rules of the RMI Office of the Registrar of Corporations; the RMI is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961, with apostilles issued by the competent RMI authority for authenticated corporate and notarial documents. Nominee shareholders or directors are permissible only where a licensed resident agent maintains complete UBO records accessible to the FIU upon demand.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport of each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), director, shareholder, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport or civil registry authority of the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; where the issuing country is not party to the Hague Apostille Convention, full consular legalization through the RMI-representative consular channel

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or banking institution of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization (as applicable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming account conduct and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home or correspondent bank of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if issued by a non-Apostille-state bank, consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of wealth and source of funds declaration, signed under oath
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (BCCA), Republic of the Marshall Islands, Title 54 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code, as amended, particularly the provisions concerning Articles of Incorporation, registered office/agent, directors, and officers.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Majuro Atoll
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; no escrow account or capital deposit required for a non-resident Business Corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation, as filed with the Registrar of Corporations, are hereby accepted and ratified; that the subscription for the Corporation's authorized common shares, as reflected in the share register, is approved; that the registered office and registered agent appointed in the Articles are confirmed; that [Name] be and hereby is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, each to serve until their successors are duly elected; and that the said officers are authorized to execute all consents, filings, and ancillary instruments required to effectuate the Corporation's lawful business and governance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations via a licensed registered agent or direct submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search and reservation request through the registered agent. The proposed corporate name must contain a corporate designator such as 'Corporation', 'Inc.', or 'Ltd.' and must not conflict with any existing registered name.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected on grounds of identity or confusing similarity, an alternative name is submitted; the reservation can be renewed or amended without penalty if submitted promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations (via licensed registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Articles of Incorporation providing corporate name, registered office in Marshall Islands, registered agent name and address, purpose, authorized share structure, and incorporator details. Sign the Articles before a notary or appropriate witness and deliver to the registered agent for filing.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copy of each incorporator/director
Proof of residential address of each incorporator/director
Bank reference or due diligence questionnaire where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query or rejection for incomplete or defective Articles, the registered agent corrects the defect and file an amended Article or supplemental statement; expedited filing may be requested upon payment of the applicable expedited fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review of the Articles, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation. The registered agent will retrieve the certificate and confirm the corporate number and effective date.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If certificate issuance is delayed due to registry backlog or verification issues, the registered agent may follow up with the Corporations Office or apply for an expedited issuance service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation governance and initial board action
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal corporate records; corporate minutes maintained at registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold a first board meeting or execute written consent in lieu of meeting. Adopt bylaws, issue shares to subscribers, ratify the registered office and registered agent, appoint officers (President, Secretary, Treasurer), and approve tax/resident agent arrangements if applicable.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution or written consent
Share subscription records and share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a consents or bylaws contain a procedural irregularity, the board may adopt a curative resolution with retroactive effect, subject to the Corporation Act and the Corporation's governing law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - non-resident mail-order retail and e-commerce business has no industrial manufacturing establishment in the Marshall Islands
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for the offshore business corporation; a local business license would only arise from physical operations within the Marshall Islands, which are not contemplated

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - non-manufacturing commercial activity; no requirement for an Environmental Impact Assessment or registration
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, airborne emissions, or hazardous waste streams are generated by the ordertaking and logistics-settlement platform; applicability of EPA standards remains a nil obligation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable in the absence of physical premises; if a warehouse or local fulfillment office is opened later, fire safety certification and the Marshall Islands Occupational Safety and Health requirements will become mandatory.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Treasury and Revenue Administration, Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands; official portal: https://www.rmi.gov.mh/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Marshall Islands does not levy corporate income tax, VAT, or GST, and no general tax identification number is issued to non-resident Business Corporations. A non-resident Business Corporation obtains its corporate registration number from the Registrar of Corporations under the Business Corporations Act; no separate tax registration is required for offshore/non-resident operations. If the entity engages in local business activities, a business license and employer registration with the Marshall Islands Social Security Administration may be required, with registration through the relevant ministry portals.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box, hybrid mismatch, or entity-tax election is available under Marshall Islands law. The jurisdiction imposes no income tax on non-resident Business Corporations, so no domestic entity classification election exists. A U.S. federal check-the-box election under IRC Section 7701 is not a Marshall Islands statutory mechanism and would apply only to a separate U.S. tax return filer.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST or general sales and use tax; indirect taxation is limited to customs import duties and excisable goods duties under the Customs Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — no VAT or GST registration threshold exists because no such tax is levied; customs registration may be required only for import/export activities
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. The Marshall Islands does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API-linked e-invoicing, or digital stamping for invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable. Because the Marshall Islands does not impose VAT or GST, there is no statutory regime for a 0% export VAT rate, no export VAT refund mechanism, and no VAT registration from which a zero-rated supply could be claimed. Exports by non-resident Business Corporations are simply outside the domestic direct tax and indirect tax net.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration as prescribed by the Marshall Islands Customs Act
Bill of lading or airway bill evidencing physical export
Inward remittance or payment evidence where the underlying sale is settled via cross-border funds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT/GST export zero-rating clawback applies because no such tax exists. However, false customs declarations, fraudulent export documentation, and money laundering-connected invoicing are subject to Marshall Islands customs-law penalties and criminal code sanctions, which may include fines, seizure, imprisonment, and retrospective denial of claimed export duty exemptions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of the Marshall Islands does not maintain a central bank or a statutory exchange-control authority. The United States dollar is the sole legal tender by virtue of the Compact of Free Association with the United States, and monetary conditions are effectively governed by U.S. Federal Reserve policy. Banking and prudential supervision is exercised by the Financial Institutions Supervisory Division of the Ministry of Finance under the Banking Act 1990, while AML/CFT supervision is vested in the Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit pursuant to the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2012 (34 MIRC). Foreign-exchange rule-making is not separately codified; regulatory constraint arises indirectly through bank licensing conditions, FATF grey-list enhanced due diligence, and correspondent-bank counterparty policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full currency convertibility applies on both the capital and current accounts. The MH Business Corporation may receive, hold, and repatriate USD without central bank permit, exchange-control approval, or reinvestment requirement. Capital account: equity contributions, shareholder loans, and proceeds of liquidation are freely remittable. Current account: e-commerce sales receipts and COD collections may be settled in USD or converted into foreign currency at will. The only material hurdle is documentary: because the RMI is under FATF increased monitoring, remittance channels require a distilled evidence trail (underlying invoice, sales platform report, shareholder resolution) to satisfy foreign correspondent banks. Profit remittance is unrestricted under Marshall Islands law, but the paying institution will apply enhanced due diligence to amounts exceeding USD 50,000 per instruction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender rules, conversion ratios, or repatriation timelines exist under Marshall Islands law. Cross-border e-commerce receipts and mail-order export collections may be retained in USD offshore, converted at market rate, or held in multi-currency accounts without mandatory conversion. The Banking Act 1990 imposes no foreign-currency surrender obligation. In practice, the local bank or fintech EMI will require a commercial invoice or logistics manifest to distinguish trade proceeds from unlawful proceeds, and will monitor aggregate monthly inflows for consistency with the declared COD e-commerce business volume.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Current Account with correspondent clearing via U.S. partner banks
Development-finance escrow and facilitation account; not a full transactional treasury account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-rated viability with material conditions. Airwallex, as an APAC-regulated non-bank payments institution, can serve as the primary cross-border clearing and FX venue for the MH BC, subject to: (i) production of the Business Corporations Act registration certificate and good-standing extract; (ii) identification of natural-person ultimate beneficial owners with apostilled identity documents; (iii) execution of an enhanced-risk merchant acceptance agreement reflecting the FATF grey-list status of RMI; and (iv) quantitative transaction limits, typically USD 25,000 single-payment and USD 250,000 monthly velocity, expandable on submission of audited sales reports. Legal constraint: no EMI holds an RMI banking licence, so the entity remains a client of an offshore-regulated intermediary rather than a domestic depositor; funds held with the EMI are not protected by RMI deposit insurance or the U.S. FDIC, and the EMI may suspend payouts if RMI's FATF grey-listing persists or if the target emerging-market corridor triggers its own central bank restrictions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement under Marshall Islands company law mandates physical attendance of directors to open an account; remote onboarding is legally permissible. BOMI permits fully remote opening for shareholder and director natural persons holding a verified KYC profile in CONTA/USABLE identity systems, but requires a live audiovisual interview with the compliance officer. Airwallex similarly mandates an interactive video KYC session with the beneficial owner and the appointed director; substitution by the registered agent alone is disallowed. If any ultimate beneficial owner is a citizen or tax resident of a jurisdiction on the FATF grey list, physical presence before a notary public with apostille is de facto required by the onboarding bank. Effective recommendation: conduct one founding director's notarized identity verification at a U.S. consulate or regional hub (Majuro, Honolulu, or Manila) to eliminate interview delay.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdiction-risk flag: the Republic of the Marshall Islands is publicly listed under FATF increased monitoring, automatically triggering enhanced due diligence and a possible automatic decline by compliance engines of BOMI, Airwallex, and U.S. respondents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (i) current registry certificate issued by the RMI Registrar of Corporations, (ii) certificate of good standing, (iii) registered-agent confirmation, (iv) a signed beneficial-ownership declaration with full natural-person disclosures supporting the statutory register, (v) a substance narrative describing the COD e-commerce operating model, (vi) no-bearer-shares undertaking, and (vii) a written acknowledgment that all transactions will flow through FATF-compatible AML monitoring with audit rights reserved to the financial institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: nominee-director layers, bearer-share documentation, or a less-than-25% attributable ownership chain for any material shareholder triggers secondary refusal at correspondent-bank level.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the statutory beneficial-ownership register extract, corporate shareholder ledger certified by the registered agent, passport copies of each natural-person shareholder, proof of residential address, and a chain-of-control diagram. Where an intermediate vehicle appears, append charter documents and consolidated ownership tables to reduce attribution to natural persons; banks typically require the identity of every natural person holding more than 10%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Product-risk red flag: cash-on-delivery e-commerce is classified as Medium-Risk_Enhanced merchant acquiring, carrying concerns over layered cash collection, potential fraud-to-money-laundering nexus, and cross-border settlement via local logistics partners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble (i) executed merchant-remittance agreement with the logistics partner in the emerging-market corridor, (ii) six months of platform sales records or pre-launch volume model, (iii) published coding of ISIC 4791 activities with no statutory licence requirement, (iv) platform-level AML policy incorporating negative screening of COD customers and transaction-velocity thresholds, and (v) audit-ready sales-invoice trail mapped to each expected inbound remittance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Recommended compliant protocol: the founding investor wires USD from a regulated bank account to the Airwallex USD treasury wallet or BOMI current account using SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'G121 – Shareholder contribution / paid-in capital (no external approval required under RMI law)'. The swift message must include the MH Business Corporation full legal name, Meridian/Registry number, and the investor's bank reference. Verification stack consists of: (i) shareholder-ledger reconciliation, (ii) notarized source-of-funds statement for injections above USD 50,000, and (iii) declaration that no bearer shares are outstanding. Because RMI imposes no capital-approval or exchange-control filing, no central bank authorization is needed; however, the receiving institution will apply a 5-business-day clearing hold on first inbound payment pending EDD completion.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) domestic USD clearing through BOMI via ACH/telegraphic transfer to local suppliers and logistics partners; (2) cross-border supplier and vendor payments via SWIFT MT103 routed through BOMI's U.S. correspondent chain, with mandatory remittance advice quoting the underlying purchase order and ISIC 4791 invoice; (3) commercial letters of credit issued by BOMI's global correspondent for bulk inventory replenishment, on the order of USD 250,000 outbound, requiring a pro-forma invoice and transport document; (4) Airwallex payout-API rail for high-frequency, low-value disbursements to the emerging-market logistics remittance partner, using virtual account numbers and local clearing (instant settlement into the partner's local bank account). All outbound instructions must carry the purpose code 'TRADE-GOODS/EPAYMENT' distinct from the AML narrative, and per-transaction amounts above USD 100,000 require appended director's resolution and economic-substance declaration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EM-local-currency deliverable forwards with authorized bank counterparty, tenure up to six months, hedged against forecast COD settlement flows
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the emerging-market target currency, cash-settled in USD, for currencies with non-convertible or restricted onshore delivery
Cross-currency swaps (USD versus EM-local-currency) matched against offsetting trade receivables and logistics settlement cycles, mark-to-market limit equal to three months of projected inflows

Plain vanilla USD call / EM put options for downside protection of the COD reload cycle; exotic digital, accumulator, and barrier structures prohibited unless separately approved by the treasury committee

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report and Franchise Tax Filing to the Marshall Islands Corporate Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Majuro)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on the anniversary of the date of incorporation each calendar year; a 3-month administrative grace period applies before penalty accrual; filing is completed by the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of 10% of the annual report fee assessed after the 3-month grace period; failure to file for two consecutive annual periods authorizes the Registrar to administratively dissolve the corporation and strike its name from the Corporate Registry

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Continuation Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Marshall Islands Registered Agent (no public filing required where the agent and office remain unchanged)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annexed to the annual report cycle; immediate written notification to the Registrar is required within 21 days of any change of registered agent or registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Uninterrupted failure to maintain a resident registered agent and office constitutes a ground for involuntary administrative dissolution under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act; agent resignation without replacement triggers Registrar action

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Reporting Declaration (if operating outside the tax-exempt safe harbor)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations (economic substance filing channel)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 12 months of the corporation's fiscal year end; applies only if the entity has Marshall Islands domestic-source income or a physical local presence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A non-resident tax-exempt corporation with no local activity is outside the reporting obligation; erroneous non-filing with local activity carries penalties of up to US$10,000 and possible strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandated for non-resident Business Corporations under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act; an independent audit becomes compulsory only when triggered by a shareholder resolution, lender covenant, court order, or commencement of domestic Marshall Islands revenue-generating activity
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or US GAAP may be adopted; no Marshall Islands Local GAAP exists for non-resident exempt corporations; financial statements are not required to be filed with the Registrar and are retained solely by the entity and its registered agent

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Business Corporations (Amendment) Act 2019, the corporation must maintain a private beneficial ownership register at its registered office, kept by the licensed agent; the agent must conduct an annual confirmation refresh concurrent with the annual report cycle and must be notified of any share transfer or UBO change within 30 days; the register is non-public and is disclosed only to the Registrar or authorized law-enforcement bodies on lawful request
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges (Security Interests and Mortgages)
Minute Book of Shareholder and Director Meetings
Private Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$650 - US$1,200 per annum covering the licensed registered agent, registered office, and annual report processing
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$0 where no voluntary audit is engaged; US$2,500 - US$6,000 per annum for an optional certified audit of a single-entity e-commerce holding structure

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for a non-resident domestic Business Corporation (BC); the RMI Income Tax Act imposes tax only on income sourced within the Marshall Islands, and this entity is structured as a non-resident tax-exempt BC. The nominal resident corporate rate on RMI-source taxable income is 15%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Automatic statutory exemption from RMI corporate income tax on foreign-source income; no capital gains tax, no dividend distribution tax, no branch profit or remittance tax, and no RMI payroll social security tax for employees located outside the Marshall Islands. No tax holiday application or ruling is required; the exemption is conferred by the non-resident domestic corporation status under the Business Corporations Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No RMI corporate income tax return is required for a non-resident BC. The only mandatory statutory filing is the BCA Annual Report, submitted through the registered agent to the Registrar of Corporations via the Marshall Islands corporate registry portal or prescribed paper form.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The BCA Annual Report is due each year on or before the anniversary date of incorporation; no quarterly or annual CIT filing is applicable while the non-resident exemption remains valid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full registered name of the Business Corporation as set forth in the certificate of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the exact registered English name; no trade name, abbreviation, or translation may be substituted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique file number assigned by the RMI Registrar of Corporations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be obtained from the certificate of incorporation or the registered agent; required for electronic registry identification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Item 3 - Registered Office and Registered Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical address in the Marshall Islands and identity of the licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident BC must continuously maintain a registered office and agent in the Republic; a post office box alone is not a sufficient registered office address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and usual residential addresses of all directors and officers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors may be non-residents and need not be physically present in RMI, but their details must be disclosed to the registered agent and reflected in the annual report.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Maximum number of shares authorized, classes and par value, and the number of shares issued and outstanding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State exact share figures in U.S. dollars; beneficial ownership information must be separately maintained by the registered agent under the AML framework.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that the corporation is not carrying on business in the Marshall Islands and has no income from sources within RMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This declaration is the factual basis for the income tax exemption. If the company commences RMI activities, the declaration becomes materially false and RMI tax filing obligations may arise.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the Annual Report and non-payment of the annual government fee trigger late charges, loss of good standing, administrative dissolution by the Registrar, and reinstatement expenses. If an RMI income tax return becomes required, late filing attracts a 5% monthly penalty up to 25%, plus statutory interest; deliberate non-filing can be prosecuted as tax evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - the Marshall Islands imposes no dividend withholding tax and no dividend distribution tax on dividends paid by a non-resident BC to non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not applicable in RMI. The Marshall Islands has no comprehensive double taxation agreement network and does not withhold on non-resident distributions, so no DTA relief application or tax-residence certificate is required at source. Where a foreign shareholder seeks a foreign tax credit or exemption in its residence jurisdiction, the shareholder should obtain from the RMI Registrar or the registered agent a certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, and any required proof of non-resident tax status.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory withholding tax on royalties and interest paid by a non-resident BC to non-residents; no treaty-lower rate is applicable because no comprehensive income tax treaty is in force.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No local currency threshold; no RMI Local File or Master File obligation exists for a non-resident tax-exempt BC. If the entity were to derive RMI-source taxable income, source-based assessment would apply and OECD-consistent transfer pricing documentation would be relevant; no statutory monetary threshold is prescribed for non-resident exempt entities.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The RMI Economic Substance (Amendment) Act and BCA-related ESR Regulations apply to non-resident domestic corporations that carry on a relevant activity. A COD mail-order/e-commerce business engaged in purchasing, inventory management, order-taking, delivery, and settlement logistics can fall within the 'distribution and service centre' relevant activity and must satisfy core income-generating activity substance requirements: local board presence or management, adequate staff and operating expenditure, and an annual ESR substance report filed through the registered agent. A purely passive non-resident BC with no relevant activity need only maintain the registered office and registered agent. Non-resident BCs that are tax resident in a foreign jurisdiction may rely on foreign tax residence, but a timely, fact-based ESR declaration is still required.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Abuse of Non-Resident Exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting actual trade or business in the Marshall Islands through local inventory, employees, customers, or RMI-source cash collection while continuing to declare non-resident status and suppressing taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of the 15% corporate income tax on all RMI-source taxable income, plus statutory interest, late-payment penalties, and fraud penalties of up to 50% of the underpayment; criminal conviction for willful tax evasion is punishable by a fine of up to US$10,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 3 years per offense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who authorize false declarations or conceal RMI-source receipts are jointly and severally liable for the tax, penalties, and enforcement costs. The corporate veil may be pierced on a showing of sham or fraud, exposing directors to civil restitution, travel bans, and criminal custodial sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the BC as a shell with no office, employees, management, or substance while carrying on COD e-commerce or distribution activities, or failing to file the Annual Report and ESR substance return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative strike-off or dissolution by the Registrar; financial penalties under the ESR Regulations for non-compliance, including daily default penalties and increased fines for false substance declarations; loss of legal capacity to enforce contracts or pursue claims while struck off.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for company debts incurred after a default leading to dissolution. In cross-border proceedings, foreign courts may disregard the RMI shell and impose liability against the true economic operator; directors and beneficial owners may face disqualification, asset freezes, and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using COD logistics and remittance settlement rails to collect or settle cash proceeds without customer due diligence, source-of-funds verification, or beneficial-ownership records; structuring cash deposits to avoid reporting thresholds; commingling merchant funds with third-party logistics payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of the RMI Money Laundering (Prevention and Control) Act 2011, as amended: criminal fines of up to US$100,000 per offense, imprisonment of up to 10 years, confiscation of proceeds of crime, and civil penalties for non-compliance with registered-agent and AML record-keeping duties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, nominee directors, and compliance officers who knowingly facilitate or remain willfully blind to COD-settlement laundering are personally criminally liable; the corporate veil does not protect deliberate AML violations. Enforcement measures include civil restitution, asset freezing, travel bans, and extradition or prosecution under international cooperation arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Registry Filings and Beneficial Ownership Misrepresentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing an Annual Report or ESR declaration that falsely states the non-resident status, hides the identity of the ultimate beneficial owner, or misrepresents the location where e-commerce management decisions are made.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: False statement offenses under the Business Corporations Act: fines of up to US$5,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 6 months; cancellation of good standing; monetary penalties for late or incomplete beneficial-ownership disclosure to the registered agent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve a false filing are personally liable for damages suffered by creditors or third parties relying on the registry record. Disqualification from serving as a director and travel bans may be imposed in the context of cross-border insolvency or AML investigations.
